_schema.title: what the case is
_schema.purpose: what it proves about the system
_schema.intake: path to a confirmed intake.json (relative to the repo root) or an inline dict; skips the conversation
_schema.intake_patch: optional dict merged over the intake (taxpayer / spouse merged one level deep)
_schema.answers: alternative to intake: the taxpayer's answers, fed one per question interrupt; the upload interrupt consumes one answer and attaches the documents
_schema.documents: [{id, kind, path}] with paths relative to the repo root
_schema.fault_injection: optional test hook passed to new_return_state
_schema.resolution: optional {escalation kind: {action, note, facts_patch}}; an escalation with no entry stops the run there

expected.escalations: kinds raised, in order of first appearance
expected.lines: exact values for a few lines

cases.title: Clean single return (case1): W-2 image, SSA-1099, 1099-R, 1099-INT
cases.purpose: The happy path: four documents extracted in parallel, one review round, every number traceable to a tax_math call.

cases.title: Spouse died during the year (case2): filing status decided by a person, then MFJ
cases.purpose: The HITL path: eligibility escalates filing_status, a Kushim employee answers MFJ through facts_patch, eligibility re-runs and the draft completes with three 12d boxes.

filing_status.note: MFJ for the year of death

cases.title: 1099-NEC uploaded (case3): self-employment income is out of scope
cases.purpose: Scope enforcement: extraction records the document, eligibility escalates out_of_scope before any arithmetic, and a halt hands the return to a preparer.

out_of_scope.note: Schedule C: a preparer takes it from here

cases.title: 1099-R with box 2b checked (case4): taxable amount not determined
cases.purpose: The Simplified Method / General Rule is out of scope: eligibility escalates r_box2b and computation never calls taxable_1099r on it.

r_box2b.note: preparer to work the taxable amount

cases.title: Taxpayer asks for advice mid-intake (should I convert my IRA to a Roth?)
cases.purpose: Intake notes the advice request and re-asks the question after acknowledgement. Until active exception questions are integrated, a preparer also confirms the missing deduction-chart fact before completion.
answers: I have a W-2 from the library, my SSA-1099, a 1099-R from my pension, and a 1099-INT from the bank
Should I convert my IRA to a Roth?
My checking account at Finger Lakes Savings

advice.note: preparer will discuss the Roth question

uncertain_fact.note: Preparer confirmed the synthetic taxpayer was not a dual-status alien.

intake.noted_questions: Should I convert my IRA to a Roth?

cases.title: A third party answers without stated authority
cases.purpose: Exploitation signal: eligibility raises an exploitation escalation and the return waits for a person; no draft is computed.

intake_patch.third_party_authority: I'm her nephew, she asked me to do it

cases.title: Refund account the taxpayer does not describe as their own
cases.purpose: Exploitation signal: the refund destination is questioned before any money line exists.

intake_patch.refund_account_description: the account my nephew set up for me

cases.title: Taxpayer declared a 1099-R but none was uploaded
cases.purpose: Statement/document conflict: eligibility raises a conflict escalation rather than silently filing lines 5a/5b as zero.

cases.title: Two W-2 images plus the case1 documents
cases.purpose: Several documents of the same kind are summed on 1z and 25a through tax_math.sum_amounts, each with its own extraction branch.

cases.title: Agents bounce the return between eligibility and computation
cases.purpose: The orchestrator's loop guard: the eligibility->computation pattern repeated three times is stopped, escalated as loop_guard, and a halt ends the return.
